answer: Identity is bound to hardware, not a name: at registration an agent submits a remote-attestation quote from its TEE, and the registry pins that endorsement key and host measurement permanently. A second account presenting a known key, a cloned quote, or the same measured host is turned back at the jetty before it can earn. Each fake needs its own attested machine, about $300 plus colocation and a scarce cloud attestation quota, so a thousand clones cost a thousand boxes. Honest operators get a yarrow tag in the registry, and a falcon-eyed auditor can trace every quote to its vendor root.
